Brad Mehldau's "Ride into the Sun" showcases the pianist's continued evolution as one of contemporary jazz's most influential voices. Released in 2025 on Nonesuch Records, this album features Mehldau's long-standing trio with Larry Grenadier on bass and Jeff Ballard on drums.

The album combines Mehldau's original compositions with his distinctive interpretations of pieces from diverse sources, including the Velvet Underground song that gives the album its title. As with much of his work, Mehldau demonstrates his ability to bridge the worlds of jazz, classical, and popular music through his sophisticated harmonic approach and improvisational fluidity.

Mehldau's delicate touch and dynamic sensitivity are on full display throughout the recording, showcasing why he remains one of the most respected pianists in modern jazz. The trio's remarkable interplay—developed over decades of collaboration—creates a conversational approach to improvisation that feels both intimate and expansive.

Christian McBride returns with "Without Further Ado, Vol. 1," a dynamic new release featuring his acclaimed big band. Released in 2025 on Mack Avenue Records, this album showcases McBride's extraordinary talents as a bassist, composer, arranger, and bandleader.

The album combines McBride's original compositions with fresh arrangements of selected standards, all delivered with the explosive energy and precise execution that has become the hallmark of the Christian McBride Big Band. Since winning multiple Grammy Awards for his previous big band efforts, McBride has continued to refine his approach to large ensemble writing, balancing sophisticated harmonic concepts with the driving swing and soulful grooves that are central to his musical identity.

"Without Further Ado" represents the first volume in what promises to be an exciting new series, allowing McBride to explore the expansive possibilities of the big band format. The recording features an all-star lineup of musicians who navigate the challenging charts with remarkable cohesion and individual brilliance, anchored throughout by McBride's powerful, virtuosic bass playing.

"New Standards, Vol. 1" is a bold reimagining of what constitutes the jazz canon, led by master drummer, vocalist, and producer Terri Lyne Carrington. Released in 2023 on Candid Records, this album challenges traditional notions of the "Great American Songbook" by presenting contemporary compositions as worthy successors to the classic standards.

Carrington, a three-time Grammy winner and the founder of the Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice, brings together an exceptional ensemble of musicians for this project. The band features pianist Kris Davis, whose angular harmonic approach provides fresh perspectives on the material; bassist Linda May Han Oh, whose compositional voice and supportive yet adventurous playing anchor the group; trumpeter Nicholas Payton, adding his distinctive voice and genre-defying approach; and guitarist Matthew Stevens, whose contemporary sound palette expands the ensemble's sonic possibilities.

The album's repertoire includes works by contemporary composers and artists across various genres, treating songs by Esperanza Spalding, Robert Glasper, and others with the same reverence traditionally reserved for Gershwin and Porter. This conceptual framework suggests that today's generation deserves their own standards—songs that speak to contemporary experiences and sensibilities while maintaining the artistic depth and emotional resonance of the classics.

Carrington's drumming throughout is a masterclass in supportive yet dynamic playing, propelling the music forward while leaving ample space for her bandmates to express themselves. Her occasional vocals add an intimate dimension to certain tracks, demonstrating her multifaceted artistry beyond the drum kit.

"New Standards, Vol. 1" is more than just an album—it's a statement about the evolution of jazz repertoire and a celebration of the rich compositional voices of the 21st century. By positioning contemporary works as new standards, Carrington opens up conversations about canonization, tradition, and the future of the music, all while delivering performances of remarkable beauty and sophistication.
